privacy.body.changes: If we make a material change to how we handle your data, we'll notify registered Users before it takes effect and update the version and date at the top of this page.
privacy.body.children: Work4U is not directed at, and may not be used by, anyone under 18. We don't knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we'll remove it.
privacy.body.contact: Questions about this policy, or to exercise any of the rights in Section 8, contact privacy@work4u.app
privacy.body.controller: Work4U is the data controller for the personal data described in this policy. Work4U is currently operated as an individually-run online service rather than through an incorporated company; contact details are in Section 13. If Work4U is incorporated, this section will be updated to name that entity as controller.
privacy.body.cookies: We use a strictly necessary session cookie to keep you signed in and route you correctly between signed-in and signed-out pages. It doesn't track you across other sites and isn't used for advertising. If we add analytics or marketing cookies in future, we'll ask for your consent first, as required by law, and update this section.
privacy.body.howWeUse:
We use your data to:

  • operate your account and the core matching, messaging, and review features;
  • verify identity signals (email, phone) and investigate reports or suspected policy violations;
  • send service messages (account, security, Job-related notifications) and, if you've opted in, product updates;
  • maintain a record that you accepted our Terms and this Policy, and when; and
  • understand aggregate usage so we can fix problems and prioritise what to build next.
privacy.body.legalBases:
Under GDPR Article 6, we rely on the following legal bases:

  • Performance of a contract — creating your account, matching you with Jobs, running chat and reviews.
  • Legitimate interests — preventing fraud and abuse, improving the Platform, and maintaining safety features like reporting and suspension, balanced against your right to privacy.
  • Consent — where we ask separately, such as optional marketing communications; you can withdraw this at any time.
  • Legal obligation — where we must retain or disclose data to comply with the law.
privacy.body.retention: We keep account and Job data for as long as your account is active, plus a limited period afterwards to resolve disputes, comply with legal obligations, and prevent banned users from simply re-registering. When you delete your account, we deactivate it and schedule the underlying personal data for erasure, subject to any data we're legally required to retain for longer (for example, billing records).
privacy.body.rights:
Under GDPR, you have the right to:

  • access the personal data we hold about you;
  • rectify inaccurate or incomplete data;
  • erase your data (“right to be forgotten”), subject to legal retention limits;
  • restrict or object to certain processing, including profiling based on legitimate interests;
  • port your data to another service in a structured, machine-readable format;
  • withdraw consent at any time, where processing is based on consent; and
  • lodge a complaint with the data protection authority in your country of residence.

Most of these can be exercised directly from your profile settings; for anything else, contact us using the details in Section 13.
privacy.body.security: We use reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect your data, including encrypted connections and access controls on our database and admin tools. No system is perfectly secure, so if you become aware of a vulnerability, please report it to us responsibly using the contact details below.
privacy.body.sharing:
We share the minimum necessary data with service providers who process it on our behalf (as processors, under Article 28 GDPR):

  • Firebase / Google Cloud — authentication and, if configured, analytics.
  • Our database host — stores account, Job, and message data.
  • Image hosting provider (ImgBB) — stores photos you choose to upload; note that uploaded images are hosted on ImgBB's public infrastructure, so avoid uploading images containing sensitive personal information you wouldn't want broadly accessible.
  • Stripe — processes subscription payments if you upgrade to Work4U Pro.
  • A translation API — used to auto-translate chat messages between Users where language differs.

We do not sell your personal data. We may disclose data where required by law, to protect the rights or safety of Users or the public, or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or asset sale — in which case we'll tell affected Users.

Other Users see the profile, listing, review, and message content you choose to share with them as a normal part of using the Platform — that's inherent to how a marketplace works, not a third-party disclosure.
privacy.body.transfers: Some of the providers listed in Section 5 may process data outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States. Where that happens, we rely on the provider's Standard Contractual Clauses or an equivalent safeguard recognised under GDPR Chapter V.
privacy.body.whatWeCollect:
• Account data — name, email, phone number, password (via Firebase Authentication), profile photo.
  • Profile & listing data — bio, skills, hourly rate, service area, location/address, job postings and applications.
  • Communications — messages you send through in-app chat, including images shared in a conversation.
  • Reputation data — reviews and ratings you give or receive, reports you file or are named in.
  • Engagement data — activity used to power account levels, achievements, and quests within the Platform.
  • Payment data — for a paid subscription, billing details are collected directly by our payment processor (Stripe); Work4U does not store your card details.
  • Device & usage data — device type, browser, operating system, pages visited, and how you were referred to the Platform.

terms.body.definitions:
• “Account” means your registered Work4U profile.
  • “Job” means a task, service, or piece of work posted, offered, or agreed between a Requester and a Worker through the Platform.
  • “Content” means anything you submit to the Platform, including job listings, service listings, messages, images, reviews, and profile information.
  • “User” / “you” means anyone with a Work4U account, whether acting as a Requester, a Worker, or both.
terms.body.disputes: If something goes wrong with a Job or another User's conduct, use the in-app “Report” / “Dispute this job” tool available from the Job page or chat conversation. This flags the matter for review; a Job under an active dispute may be marked accordingly while it's looked into. We review reports in good faith and may request information from both sides, but we are not a court or an ombudsman — for a Job-level disagreement (unpaid work, damaged property, quality of work), the underlying legal responsibility remains between the Requester and the Worker under Section 4. terms.body.natureOfService:
Work4U is a venue, not a party to your Job. We provide the tools that let Requesters and Workers find each other, communicate, agree terms, and rate one another afterwards. When a Requester and a Worker agree to a Job, the contract for that Job — including its scope, price, timing, quality, and safety — is directly between the two of them. Work4U is not:

  • an employer, staffing agency, or contractor of either party;
  • a guarantor of any Job's completion, quality, legality, or safety;
  • a party to, or a processor of payment for, the underlying Job itself (see Section 7); or
  • responsible for verifying every claim a User makes in a listing, profile, or message, beyond the checks described in these Terms.

We do provide tools intended to raise trust — profile and contact verification steps, in-app messaging, a reporting and dispute-flagging system, and account suspension for Users who violate these Terms — and we describe those honestly. But using Work4U does not replace your own judgment: check who you're dealing with, agree the details in writing through the Platform, and use common sense before letting someone into your home or handing over payment.

Payment for the Job itself — what a Requester pays a Worker for the work performed — is currently arranged directly between the Requester and the Worker, outside the Platform. If and when Work4U introduces in-platform payment or escrow for Jobs, this section will be updated before that feature goes live, and separate payment terms will apply to it.
